newsitem.title: POLAND: Salomon Brothers sees Polish rating upgrade soon.
newsitem.headline: Salomon Brothers sees Polish rating upgrade soon.

text.p: Salomon Brothers expects Poland's sovereign debt rating to be upgraded as early as the forth quarter of 1997, it said in a report dated May 28.
"Poland could receive an one-notch upgrade from one of the major rating agencies, most likely Standard & Poor's, in the fourth quarter of 1997," Salomon said.
"(Poland) has potential to ascend to the upper tier of the triple-B ratings grade within two or three years." it said.
On Tuesday Standard & Poor's affirmed Poland's sovereign rating of BBB- and changed the outlook from stable to positive.

Analysts said that if this September's parliamentary polls yield a stable government which would continue pro-market economic policies, Poland was likely to get an upgrade from the next Standard & Poor's evaluation.
Salomon said it based the positive assessment on continued development of democracy, increased integration with the West and larger external flexibility of Poland.

It also said Poland needed to continue to pursue tight fiscal and monetary policies, adopt measures to limit the recent deterioration of its external accounts and tackle politically sensitive pension reform. -- Warsaw Newsroom +48 22 653 9700
